observations: Public CLI validates request digest, normalized no-symlink paths, absent output, private owned empty output parent, bound records, one-attempt field, fixed case and maximum compile/deadline window before launch. Launcher approval does not replace the separate builder source approval.

quota_run mounts private tmpfs over the exact output parent. The pre-overlay host descriptor is non-inheritable and is passed only to the later bind mount. The mirror is absent during compiler execution.

Nested PID namespace init exit kills detached descendants before unshare returns. Retention starts only afterwards. Actual Linux tests showed a double-forked setsid descendant cannot perform its delayed host write.

Retention preflights every entry, rejects nonregular and multiply linked files, sums logical sizes, uses no-follow identity-checked descriptors and bounded streaming with a shared quota. Sparse logical sizes are counted. Actual namespace tests show ENOSPC and exact original-path restoration.

Cleanup preserves retention failure plus both unmount failures in an exception group, and preserves a nonzero primary child exit when cleanup also fails. Any such error prevents a successful wrapper status.

Root-provided actual local systemd probe receipt shows a SIGTERM-ignoring inert process terminated by SIGKILL after 1.008 seconds with RuntimeMaxSec=1, TimeoutStopUSec=0, SendSIGKILL=yes, FinalKillSignal=9 and an empty terminal ControlGroup. This resolves the suspected zero-to-infinity ambiguity on this machine. Reviewer inspected and hash-bound the probe receipt; reviewer did not execute that service.

Exact production-source delta against hash-verified prior launcher is two lines after successful bind mount: os.fstat(host) and mirror.stat() device/inode equality is required before retain. The original descriptor references the pre-overlay host directory; a wrong mount destination now fails before writing retained bytes.

Mirrored is set before the identity check, so identity mismatch follows existing unmount and grouped-error cleanup. This strengthens successful-command-status evidence without changing resource limits or child execution.

The current 13-test suite passed including that regression and real Linux namespace tests. Cleanup fault test now supplies correct mocked mount identity to reach its intended injected retention failure.
